note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 223, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: GER 1ST & 2ND ARMIES stays a combined local formation; do not invent a post-1871 German Empire identity.

The departmental museum director’s account identifies Bazaine’s imperial army in the Mars-la-Tour/Rezonville fighting. The Gravelotte municipal account documents the 8th line infantry in this Army of the Rhine and Lanquetin’s death on 16 August, with the precise spot near Rezonville uncertain. Together these support an explicitly representative line-infantry component of the mixed army, without claiming a precise deployment, regiment-wide uniform or infantry proportion. The CDB label FR ARMY OF LORRAINE is retained. The kepi, blue-grey campaign capote, garance trousers and Chassepot M1866 with sabre bayonet are a documented 1870 line-infantry analogy. Clothing, regiment, supply and branch varied; this is not a claim that every soldier of the mixed army wore or carried these items. Zouaves, tirailleurs, guards, mobiles, cavalry and artillery are not converted into line infantry. No component proportion, new participant, strength, loss or death is inferred. The Draner print used for visual corroboration was published in 1871; it is not dated to the battle and does not broaden the profile’s eligibility.

The institutional Deutsche Biographie entry for Buddenbrock identifies him as a Prussian general commanding the 6th Infantry Division in Alvensleben’s III Corps of the Second Army, and explicitly describes that division fighting at Vionville–Mars-la-Tour on 16 August 1870. This establishes one Prussian infantry component within the unchanged GER 1ST & 2ND ARMIES aggregate, not the uniform of every formation. The leather spiked helmet, blue tunic, grey trousers and Dreyse M1862 form a representative 1870 Prussian line-infantry analogy. Helmet patterns, regimental details, clothing and equipment varied. The Auxonne helmet is a surviving November 1870 trophy, not an object proven to have been at this battle; the Carnavalet print shows several forms of dress. No fixed bayonet or precise regimental badge is reconstructed. The equipment identity Q27306 is a gate for this reviewed component only. Existing participant IDs, names, aggregate membership, all strengths, losses and deaths remain unchanged; no infantry share is inferred. Cavalry, artillery, guards, riflemen and allied states are not recategorized as this line-infantry component.
